title: Chronic Lack of Sleep is Associated With Increased Sports Injuries in Adolescent Athletes
authors: Milewski MD, Skaggs DL, Bishop GA, Pace JL, Ibrahim DA, Wren TA, Barzdukas A
population: Adolescent middle/high-school athletes (mean age 15 y, range 12-18)
findings: 112 adolescent athletes (70% completion rate; 54 male, 58 female) completed an online survey, correlated with a retrospective review of school injury records.
Hours of sleep per night and grade in school were the best independent predictors of injury in multivariate analysis.
Athletes sleeping on average <8 hours per night were 1.7 times more likely to have had an injury than those sleeping >=8 hours (95% CI 1.0-3.0; P = 0.04).
Each additional grade in school made injury 1.4 times more likely (95% CI 1.2-1.6; P < 0.001).
limitations: Adolescent multi-sport sample, cross-sectional with retrospective injury data and self-reported sleep; association not causation; CI lower bound is 1.0; not run-specific and not adult.
implications: Supports chronic short sleep as a soft injury-risk input for explanatory copy only; do not hard-code the 8 h cut-off for adults.
Not suitable for automated load cuts.
Prefer adult evidence (Walsh 2021) for any sleep rule.

verification.notes: Crossref confirms title, J Pediatr Orthop, first author Milewski, March 2014. Odds figures verified in the raw Europe PMC abstract (PMID 25028798).
